note:
Coverage. All 37 physical pages were read at text level and all 29 measured regions were inspected on a crop. Two captioned exhibits were confirmed by locating their rules in the PDF geometry instead of a crop, because they own no region: Table 3 on p17 is three horizontal rules from x 227 to 368 at y 599, 617 and 660, and Table 4 on p22 is three rules from x 194 to 401 at y 455, 473 and 573. The nineteen excluded regions are, in page order: the two unnumbered security and political equations on p7; equations (1) on p11 and (2), (3), (4) on p12; (6) and (7) on p14; (8) as a four-line block with its own constraint column on p15, together with (9) and (10); (11) on p16; (13) on p23; the pasted prose paragraph of p26; the three crops of Appendix A's screenshot on p28 and p29; and the appendix code-and-heading runs on p30 and p36. 

The census arithmetic. Twelve printed exhibits, ten measured regions for them, two captioned exhibits with no region at all, and nineteen regions that are not exhibits. That is the worst coverage ratio in this lane so far by region count and it has a single mechanical cause: a booktabs grid without a closed frame has no area, so the detector's clustering step drops it, while a pasted equation - which is artwork the census does not want - has a tall bbox and is kept. The two previous papers lost captioned exhibits to the opposite fault (artwork too small to cluster); here the loss is a rule-only grid, which is the cleanest table style in the corpus. 

Every equation is a picture. Thirteen of the nineteen exclusions are display equations dropped in as grey rasters whose equation numbers are printed INSIDE the image, so the text layer of this paper contains almost no mathematics: p15 carries section 4.6 and Equation (9) and yet its text layer holds no equation body at all. The consequence for the census is that a paper can look equation-poor in text and hold thirteen equation images, and only the region list knows. 

The pointer layer uses a format the caption layer never uses. Captions are all 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:', with colon and space, eight figures below and two tables above. The prose, without exception, prints 'Figure (2)', 'Table (1)', 'Table (2)', 'Figure (7)', 'Figure (8)' - six pointers, four distinct numbers, zero occurrences of the caption's own spelling. A detector keyed on 'Figure N' finds the captions and none of the citations, which is the same blind spot mcm-d0 hit on #270 with 'Figure.1'. Worse, both 'Figure (7)' pointers name the wrong object: the first introduces Figure 5's 3-D scatter and the second introduces Figure 6's India treemap, so the number 7 has two citations and its own chart has none. 

Three of eight figures are exotic types. Figure 1 is a four-quadrant pie disc with a 'stability index' circle over the hub - four equal slices, no numbers, no key, an icon standing in for the model's four fields. Figures 3 and 6 are two-level treemaps on the same template, and the template is not stable across them: the dark-blue column that is captioned 'Extreme' in Figure 3 is captioned 'Politics' in Figure 6, so the sibling figures cannot be compared. With the doughnut and Venn of #163 and the radar of mcm-d0's #268, that is six exotic charts in five papers: the fourteen-family vocabulary is not holding the corpus. 

One real 3-D chart, and it is wrong. Figure 5 is a perspective scatter of 178 countries on three variables with colour redundantly re-encoding the vertical axis on a cyan-to-magenta ramp whose colourbar is labelled 10 to 60 while the axis spans 0 to 80. The colour therefore means something the key cannot express, and the paper's central claim - a linear relation between the self-regulatory factor and the SPEC score, which motivates the whole tipping model - rests on a 3-D plot where the relation is hardest to read. 

Tables. Both are booktabs, but only two tables in the document measure. Table 1 is the notation grid: 26 rows, 25 symbols in five field blocks, caption printed inside the top rule so it reads as a header cell, and subscripts set two ways inside the same table (true subscripts for the security, political and economic symbols, literal underscores for the climate ones). Table 2 is the AHP output: 17 indicator rows in four blocks divided by rules rather than by a group column, a unit in the header, two-decimal values aligned on the point, and one row label corrupted to mojibake. Neither overflows the 425 pt measure. 

Apparatus. The red Taobao banner prints on five pages including one appendix page whose content is itself a screenshot. The folio runs six pages behind the physical page, the contents list claims 20 pages for a 37-page document, and the appendix's 178-country results table is a landscape page pasted sideways at about five point type, cut into three measured strips. Section 6.1.2, 'Impact of Universal Extreme Weather Probability p%', is a heading with no body: its single paragraph is a raster image, which is the only place in the lane so far where a whole prose block has been pasted rather than typeset.
